rationale: Retain one Saavi Energía platform, correct the current owner from a mislabeled BlackRock/GEPIF III row to GIP through its Emerging Markets Fund I program, preserve Actis as the former owner, and record the signed but unclosed Grupo México combination as pending. BlackRock's 2024 acquisition of GIP was a manager-parent transaction, not a Saavi asset transfer.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Saavi Energía is a Mexico-based power-generation and gas-infrastructure platform serving wholesale, commercial and industrial electricity users and gas-services customers. The platform operates more than 3.7 GW across six combined-cycle plants, one solar plant, three gas-compression stations, three mobile turbines and a 40-mile pipeline. Actis formed Saavi from the InterGen México business in 2018 and sold 100% of the platform to Global Infrastructure Partners in August 2021 through GIP's emerging-markets infrastructure program. GIP remains the current legal owner. On April 27, 2026, GIP signed an agreement to combine Saavi with Grupo México power assets; if it closes, Grupo México would own 70% and GIP 30%. No legal closing was identified through August 23, 2026.
